a1.say: Let's solve Unique ID Generator, using the Bit Packing approach.

a1.cap: Distributed systems need unique, time-sortable IDs without a central counter. IdGenerator(machine) builds 64-bit IDs as (timestamp << 22) | (machine << 12) | sequence. next(ts) receives non-decreasing timestamps; the sequence restarts at 0 for each new timestamp and increases by 1 for repeated timestamps (assume fewer than 4096 per timestamp). Return the ID.
a1.say: Distributed systems need unique, time-sortable IDs without a central counter. Id Generator(machine) builds 64-bit IDs as (timestamp shifted left by 22) | (machine shifted left by 12) | sequence. next(ts) receives non-decreasing timestamps; the sequence restarts at 0 for each new timestamp and increases by 1 for repeated timestamps (assume fewer than 4096 per timestamp). Return the ID.

a1.cap: The top bits hold the timestamp, so IDs sort by time. The middle 10 bits name the machine, so two machines never collide. The low 12 bits are a per-timestamp sequence.
Shifting each part into place and OR-ing them packs three numbers into one 64-bit integer.
Let's walk through it with the calls IdGenerator(5), next(1), next(1), next(2).

a1.cap: Time 1, machine 5 and sequence 0 pack into 4214784.
Time 1, machine 5 and sequence 1 pack into 4214785.
Time 2, machine 5 and sequence 0 pack into 8409088.
Time complexity is O(1) and extra space is O(1).
